title: Set aside (duplicate pair): Triglycerides and coronary heart disease: the EPIC-Norfolk cohort estimate (restated)
explanation: Claim A reports a statistically significant increased risk of coronary heart disease associated with higher triglyceride levels, whereas Claim B reports no significant association after adjusting for risk factors.
a_text: In the EPIC-Norfolk study, the adjusted odds ratio for coronary heart disease comparing the top third with the bottom third of usual log-triglyceride values is 1.57 (95% CI, 1.10 to 2.24).
b_text: Triglyceride level is not significantly associated with coronary heart disease risk after adjustment for conventional risk factors (HR 0.99 per 1-SD higher value).
